questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My interest in the culture of the country, the weather, and the university's large offering of interesting courses in international law, EU law, etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
95 % of the information was sent by University of Milan's contact person, so that was quite nice. However, I think it would have been nice to have received more of the information at an earlier time so that one would not have had to check one's E-mail more or less every day in order to stay up to date on the next step in the process leading up to the exchange. For me personally, not knowing and just awaiting further instructions also at times was rather stressful.

The other 5 % takes some time to find when you have to navigate the website(s) of another university, but over time you get more and more familiar with their systems and websites.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All international students need to pick up their student ID card on location and also have their proof of attendance form signed, so I went to the international students' office and received assistance with this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The University of Milan offers student housing for - at least in my case - 300 € per month. It was very easy to receive an offer for student housing, as it was just a matter of requesting an offer from the university when you sent your application, and then later on choosing from a list of available student accommodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get an ATM card and get a monthly subscription for young people which costs 22 € per month so that you can always use the metro, buses, and trams in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a few problems in the housing, for example with the heating in the cold nights. But overall, also considering the extremely low price of 300 € per month, I was very satisfied.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to enter the courses' names, codes, ECTS points, and professors into a dedicated site on the UNIMIA platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always text the University of Milan international students' office or ask the course professor. However, in my case they were not always clear on whether or not I could actually attend their course. Therefore I strongly recommend asking all questions over E-mail so that everything is in writing if you run into any problems in connection to registering for the exams (which I find unlikely, but better safe than sorry).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I had no problems once I actually registered the courses. The only problems were the initial problems regarding whether or not I could attend certain courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guide which will be sent out by the University of Milan international students' office. If you are unsure if you can follow a certain course, ask the professor of the course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: To be candid, the academic level was shockingly low compared to the level at the University of Copenhagen. It took me 2 days per exam to prepare, which is extremely little time compared to the 7-10 days per exam I usually spend for courses at UCPH. Although to be fair, the law courses at the University of Milan are for the most part only 6 ECTS, whereas the ones at UCPH are usually 7,5, 10, or even 15 ECTS and thus requiring more time preparing for the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
There were only one class per course which was taught by the course professor(s). They were for the most part closer to classical lectures than seminars. 

I prefer the style of teaching at UCPH with the seminars which provides for more discussion of the readings and requires a greater degree of participation from the students of the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Workshop on Human Rights and the Ombudsman
2) International Law and International Law on Sustainable Development
3) European Monetary and Economic Law
4) Competition Law and Economics
5) Sources of Law and Fundamental Rights in AI

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: No. 3, 4, and 5. Also any courses taught by Filippo Croci and/or Luca Toffoletti.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, drinks, coffee, etc. and also public transport was less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are WhatsApp group chats where students get together for instance to play football, go to the theater, or go out to drink a beer on the weekends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible on the weekends! It is worth all of the money. If you like football, I also recommend going to the Stadio San Siro.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel as much as possible. I can recommend going to Verona, Venice, Naples, Sardinia, and Lugano. Prioritize meeting new people from other cultures and countries in the beginning of the exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: That is a complex matter, as there were definitely certain aspects of the Italian culture I did not enjoy and other aspects I absolutely loved. All in all, it was not that hard - but I found it to be very important to speak a basic level of Italian for doing everyday tasks such as grocery shopping or going for a coffee, as it is very likely that the Italian employee will not be able to speak English with you.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The Italians have no spatial awareness in the public space, so they will just be standing in the middle of a crowded room for no good reason instead of getting out of the way.

It was also very common that the professors were late to the classes, not infrequently by 10+ minutes, which was shocking to me as we in the Nordic countries consider that completely unacceptable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general kindness of the Italians and their openness to socialize, their passion for their cuisine, the language, the caffetterie and their prices, the idea of "take it slow", and their huge passion for football.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: (1) Remember to enjoy the exchange, as before you know it, it will be all over, (2) remember to register for the exams within the stated deadlines, and (3) go to Milan 1,5-2 weeks before classes start in order to get familiar with the city, meet new people, and get settled into your residence.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and establishing friendships across the European continent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting used to a completely new everyday routine in a foreign country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
